newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: FRENCH YACHTSMAN WAITING TO BE RESCUED
A stricken yachtsman is this morning floating in a life raft, about 12-hundred nautical miles off the southern coast of West Australia, waiting to be rescued.
French round-the-world sailor, Raphael Dinelli, was located last night by an RAAF Orion aircraft.
The Orion dropped a rescue kit to him, which included the liferaft, emergency supplies and a short-range radio.
The RAAF's Dave Cusworth says a rescue attempt will be made at daybreak when fellow competitor, the Aqua Quorum, is due to pass through the area.
Mr Cusworth says another Orion will go to the area, and its task will be to guide the yacht to Mr Dinelli's location.
He says Mr Dinelli appears to be in good physical condition.
HOTEL GUESTS EVECUATED IN MELBOURNE
Two hundred guests had to be evacuated from Melbourne's Centra On the Yarra hotel this morning, after fire broke out on the seventh floor.
The Fire Service says a sofa in the lobby was deliberatle lit and placed next to the lifts, causing the hotel's automatic sprinklers to activate.
A Spokesman says while there were no injuries and minimal damage was caused, there was potential for injury had someone opened the lifts at the time of the fire.
He says those evacuated were from the sixth, seventh and eighth floors.
Police are investigating.
2 OUT OF 3 BUSH FIRES UNDER CONTROL IN TASSIE
The Tasmanian Fire Service says a bushfire in the north of the State is still causing concern, while another two have been brought under control.
A bush fire at Waterhouse Point, near Tomahawk, on the north-east coast, has jumped across South Croppies Road.
Six fire units and two bulldozers are involved in fighting the blaze, which is burning in a protected National Park.
Meanwhile, nine District Fire Service units are now dampening down at a bushfire at Arthur Place in the Hawley Beach area, near Port Sorell.
The Fire Service says the fire burnt out 20 acres.
And at Cloudy Bay on South Bruny Island, three District Five Service units and Parks and Wildlife officers have now left the area, after bringing a fire under control.
They'll return early in the morning to monitor the situation.
No property damage has been caused in any of the fires.
QLD BEATS PAKISTAN IN CRICKET
The Pakistan cricket team has suffered another humiliating defeat, beaten by Queensland by 63 runs, in a day-night match in Brisbane.
Batting let Pakistan down after the had restricted Queensland to a moderate total, of eight for 186.
Queensland only reached that total thanks to a sparkling partnership of 76 between bowlers Andy Bichel and Adam Dale.
The Queensland bowlers then bundled Pakistan out for 123 with 12 overs to spare.
Adam Dale took five wickets, while Moin Khan top scored for the tourists with 27.
Pakistan will now play Australia A on Saturday night in Sydney.
SWIMMERS WARNED TO BE CAREFUL
Lifesavers have issued a warning for swimmers to surf in patrolled areas, after numerous rescues and a drowning yesterday near Wollongong, south of Sydney.
A young man is still missing after a group of people got into trouble in a rip in an unpatrolled area on Fairy Meadow Beach.
The search for the man began again at first light this morning.
Sydney surf spokesman Stephen Leahy says lifesavers around the metropolitan area have rescued more than 400 people over the past 36 hours.
Mr Leahy says many of these rescues could have been avoided if people swam at patrolled locations.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
